The CI failure this fix addresses, verbatim.

Source: GitHub Actions run 31131571948, PR #646 ("ci: the drain-fleet red was
placement, not capacity"), job "Build, Lint & Test". The PR was infra-only and
could not have caused this; master had passed the same lane 21 minutes earlier
(run 31130860635, sha 4a9fbf4d5), which is what makes it intermittent and
load-dependent rather than a regression.

Kept as a committed golden because it is the ONLY substrate against which the
claim "the fix addresses the observed defect rather than a cousin of it" can be
checked. Reverting the typed marker makes the driver produce this exact string
again (see duec_regime_detector_test.go and the marker's own tests); with no
copy of it in the tree, that identity would rest on a commit message.

If the pre-emption's wording is deliberately changed, this file is what goes
stale, and updating it is the moment to re-confirm that the reworded error is
still the same condition.

--- the loads that preceded it (7-10x slower than a healthy box) -------------
LOAD users    rows=100000 nullEmails=0 in 1m11.687s
LOAD users1   rows=100000 nullEmails=1000 in 52.289s
LOAD users50  rows=100000 nullEmails=50000 in 1m9.526s

--- the plan the failing query ran (an unindexed full scan) ------------------
EXPLAIN SELECT DISTINCT email_plain FROM users1 => Distinct(Project([EMAIL_PLAIN#2], Scan(USERS)))

--- the failure --------------------------------------------------------------
distinct_unique_elision_cost_probe_test.go:553: rows.Err "SELECT DISTINCT email_plain FROM users1": 40001: transaction read budget exhausted: the explicit transaction's reads are bound to FDB's 5-second MVCC window, which opened at the transaction's first read; commit sooner or decompose the work into smaller transactions
--- FAIL: TestFDB_DistinctUniqueElisionCostProbe (211.78s)

--- what that line number was ------------------------------------------------
At the failing revision, :553 is the timed loop's call
    sample, nulls, tooOld := duecRunInTx(t, ctx, tconn, o.query)
and NOT the `rows.Err` fatal inside duecRunInTx, because duecRunInTx calls
t.Helper(). The shape "S1-full" is SELECT DISTINCT email_plain FROM users1 —
411 ms on a healthy box, against a 4 s budget.
